The Certificate of the Reported Point

Source: R/inference.R
statmod_certificate.Rd

Reads the outer criterion at the reported point, independently of the path of the search, and returns a state ("converged", "boundary", "not converged" or "unknown") that is determined by the Newton decrement of the criterion. The result also holds the mode error of the coefficients, the hyperparameters and flat directions at a boundary, and the dimensionless readings that summary.StatmodFit() prints.

Usage

statmod_certificate(fit, tol = 0.01, flat = 0.002, edge = 8)

Arguments

fit

A StatmodFit().

tol

The largest rise, in the criterion's own units, that a certified point may still have available; see joint_decrement().

flat

The largest curvature \(\lvert A_{jj}\rvert\) of the outer criterion in a hyperparameter's free value at which that hyperparameter is reported as sitting at a boundary; for a coefficient the criterion estimates, the curvature times \(\max(1, \gamma_j^2)\), and for a free value of a matrix prior that scales with the matrix, the curvature in units of the matrix's scale (hyper_unit_scale()). It is also the largest eigenvalue, in absolute value, of a flat direction of the equilibrated curvature. It determines only the label and never the verdict; see the details.

edge

The free value beyond which a hyperparameter is reported as sitting at a boundary where no curvature can be read, and only there.

Value

A list with state ("converged", "boundary", "not converged" or "unknown"), decrement, gradient, mode_error, curvature, boundary, boundary_key, ridge and reason. ridge is a list with one named vector per flat direction of the outer curvature, over the coordinates that move along it. The verdict uses decrement, and gradient is reported beside it. curvature is "analytic" when the decrement was read against an analytic Hessian, "differenced" against one differenced from the exact gradient, "differenced criterion" when the criterion itself was differenced by refits, and NA when no curvature was read. boundary_key names the hyperparameters among the coordinates of boundary, in the key by which statmod_hyper_vcov() labels its rows; summary.StatmodFit() reads it to leave a standard error off a hyperparameter pinned at an edge. boundary_coef names the coefficients estimated on the outer criterion among the coordinates of boundary, as parameter:name, and summary.StatmodFit() reads it to leave their standard errors, tests and intervals off. The state is "not converged" also when the fit recorded a coordinate at the edge of its chart whose return raises the log-likelihood.

Three further fields are those that summary.StatmodFit() prints, and its page describes how they are read: inner and outer, each a named vector with gradient and eigen from certificate_readings() (NA where there is nothing to read), and zeros, which reads NULL where no coefficient sits at the kink of a penalty and is otherwise a named vector with ratio and n from zero_readings().

Details

The flag of an optimizer records whether a search stopped on its own rule, which describes the search and does not order fits by quality. The certificate describes the reported point and does not depend on the path that led to it.

The state comes from the rise that the criterion would still buy, and the mode error is reported beside it. That rise is the Newton decrement \(\tfrac{1}{2}g^\top A^{-1}g\) of joint_decrement(), in the criterion's own units, and tol is a threshold on it. The mode error is the number of log-likelihood units by which the coefficients lie above the penalized mode. Where an outer criterion exists, the mode error does not enter the verdict; for a model with no penalty and no coefficient estimated on a criterion there is no other reading, and the mode error against mode_error_limit() determines the state (see below).

The verdict is a threshold on the Newton decrement and not on the gradient, because the gradient of a criterion summed over \(n\) observations and \(p\) penalized coefficients depends on the model, so that a single threshold cannot serve every model. See joint_decrement(). The default tol is 1e-2. A user can see and check a report of "not converged" at a good point, whereas a user cannot check the certification of a point that is not a maximum, so the threshold is set low.

The cost of the certificate is one outer gradient, one curvature and one solve, at a point that the fit already holds. The criterion is reconstructed from fit@spec, so the reading refers to the fitted model. Where the form carries an analytic outer Hessian, the certificate does not refit. Where it does not (a criterion on the expected information for a family that does not supply the second derivative of its expected information, a model with a refreshable block or a structural term, or a penalty whose Hessian moves with the coefficients beside a structural term), the curvature is obtained by central differences of the exact gradient over the hyperparameters and the coefficients that the criterion estimates, which takes \(4(n_h + n_\gamma)\) refits. outer_curvature() records which route was taken, and the result reports it in curvature.

Where there is no outer gradient to read, the state depends on the case. A model with no penalty and no coefficient that the criterion estimates (a family of one parameter, or marginal empty), as with linpar, nl, seg, jump and jseg, has no coordinate for which an outer gradient could be read, so the only question left is whether the inner fit reached its mode. The state is "converged" when the mode error is at most mode_error_limit() and "not converged" otherwise. In every other case without an outer gradient the state is "unknown" and reason names the case: a model whose only hyperparameters are kinked (lasso, scad, mcp), which are chosen along a path because a Laplace approximation at a mode that sits on the kink has no meaning, so that the hyperparameter is the argument of a minimum over a grid; hyperparameters that are all held; hyperparameters chosen by aic(), bic() or cv(); and a model fitted with no outer criterion. "unknown" states that the certificate has no outer gradient to read and is not a report of failure to converge. With a kinked penalty the mode error is reported over the coordinates that the kink leaves free (free_of_kinks()): at a coefficient that the penalty has set to zero the score does not vanish but lies in the subdifferential, so that reading the score there would give a false mode error. A model that also carries a smooth penalty estimated by reml() or ml() has an outer gradient, which the certificate reads as usual.

A form whose criterion has no exact gradient (outer_gradient_ok() at order 1) has the criterion itself differenced by refits when it has at most two hyperparameters and no coefficient estimated on the criterion (three refits for one coordinate, nine for two), and curvature is then "differenced criterion". Otherwise the state is "unknown", and reason gives the cause. This is consistent with outer_curvature(), which differences a Hessian where the analytic one is missing, because that function differences the exact gradient.

A hyperparameter may run to an edge and belong there: on a covariate with no effect the smoothing parameter grows without bound, the criterion is flat in it, and the fit has not failed to converge. A coordinate is reported as sitting at a boundary where the criterion no longer moves with it, that is where its own curvature \(\lvert A_{jj}\rvert\) is at most flat. Such a hyperparameter has no meaningful interval, because \(1/\sqrt{A_{jj}}\) is the conditional standard error of its free value, and boundary_key gives summary.StatmodFit() the keys of these hyperparameters, so that it leaves their standard errors out.

The label is read from the curvature and not from the free value, because the size of a smoothing parameter depends on how its penalty is normalized and on the units of the response. The default flat of 2e-3 corresponds to a conditional standard error of the free value above 22.

The set of coordinates excluded from the verdict is narrower: a coordinate belongs to it exactly when it is reported at a boundary and its coord_decrement(), the rise that the coordinate would still give if it were the only one to move, is at most tol. The second condition prevents flat from determining the state: restricting a decrement to a subset of the coordinates is that same maximum under a constraint and so no larger, hence a coordinate moved out of the interior set cannot raise the quantity that determines the state. A coordinate at an edge that has not settled stays under test and is also named. Both "converged" and "boundary" are certified.

The set of reported coordinates and the set excluded from the verdict can differ: at a boundary the curvature collapses along with the gradient, so the one-coordinate reading \(g_j^2/(2A_{jj})\) is a ratio of two quantities going to zero and can be large. Such a coordinate is named and stays under test.

A coefficient that the criterion estimates beside the hyperparameters (the argument marginal of reml() and ml()) is read the same way, but its curvature is multiplied by \(\max(1, \gamma_j^2)\): it is reported at a boundary where its conditional standard error exceeds \(22\) times \(\max(1, \lvert\gamma_j\rvert)\). A coefficient carries the units of its parameter and of its covariate, which a hyperparameter's free value does not, so the bare curvature depends on those units. The ratio of the coefficient to its conditional standard error does not. The degrees of freedom of a Student \(t\) at their gaussian limit are an example of such a coordinate.

Where no curvature can be read at all (both routes fail to produce one, and the state is then "unknown") the label falls back on the free value, edge.

A ridge is a direction along which several coordinates move together while the criterion does not change, although the criterion is curved in each of those coordinates separately. It is read on the equilibrated curvature \(A/(ss')\), \(s_j = \sqrt{|A_{jj}|}\), whose eigenvalues are dimensionless. An eigenvalue of at most flat in absolute value names its eigenvector, written on the original coordinates in boundary and in ridge (see certificate_ridges()). A ridge whose own decrement is within tol leaves the verdict and the state is "boundary". A Burr XII shape that runs to its Weibull limit in one level of a factor is an example: the eigenvector moves only that level.

A fit that statmod() has recorded with a coordinate at the edge of its chart whose return raises the log-likelihood has the state "not converged" whatever the readings above give, and reason names the coordinate.

See also

statmod(), joint_decrement(), outer_curvature(), mode_error_limit(), criterion_resolution()

Examples

dd <- data.frame(x = runif(120))
dd$y <- sin(4 * dd$x) + rnorm(120, 0, 0.3)
statmod_certificate(statmod(y ~ s(x, bspline_smooth(k = 8)),
                            distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd))$state
#> [1] "converged"
